# Contributing to Awesome AI Agents

Contributions should help a reader choose a tool for a concrete job. Use concise descriptions and primary sources.

## Add or update an entry

1. Link to the official upstream repository or product documentation.
2. Describe one concrete capability and its target use case.
3. Check the canonical URL, archive status, deployment model and license information.
4. Place the entry in the closest existing category. Explain a new category before adding one.
5. Date claims about versions, prices, benchmarks, activity or adoption.
6. Record the source in the update audit when changing a time-sensitive claim.

Archived projects belong in explicitly historical material. Missing metadata should be reported as unknown. Stars are useful discovery signals; they are not a quality ranking.

## Benchmark and research claims

Link to the authors' methodology and results. Record the actual model, harness version, task suite, provider, sample size and verifier. Separate same-model comparisons from native product pairings. Distinguish observed provider charges, published prices and token-derived estimates.

A result from another configuration is research evidence for that configuration. It should not become an unconditional recommendation or a speed promise.

## Artwork

The current direction and reusable prompt are in [docs/assets/PREMIUM-PROMPT.md](../docs/assets/PREMIUM-PROMPT.md). Add alt text, generation or source provenance, and a practical export size. Do not copy another project's mascot or imply that an illustration is a screenshot of a working product.

## Check before opening a pull request

- Inspect the complete diff and preserve unrelated changes.
- Validate relative links, section anchors, tables and image paths.
- Check new external sources and use canonical project URLs.
- Preview the README at desktop and narrow widths.
- Make the PR description state the reader-visible change and verification performed.

Documentation edits do not require running the listed agents. If you add executable examples, pin their dependencies and record an actual verification result.
